authors: Cantlay JC, Martin GR, McClelland SC, Potier S, O'Brien MF, Fernandez-Juricic E, Bond AL, Portugal SJ
title: Binocular vision and foraging in ducks, geese and swans (Anatidae): electronic supplementary material and dataset
why: The open-access article lists Dendrocygna javanica and Lophodytes cucullatus (hooded merganser) among the species of its visual-field figures, but the text gives no per-species numbers; they sit in electronic supplementary table S1 and the deposited data, which the text I opened did not include.
get: open access: supplementary material and data from https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2023.1213 (Birmingham repository copy of the article: https://research.birmingham.ac.uk/files/205246669/rspb.2023.1213.pdf)

title: Vision and touch in relation to foraging and predator detection: insightful contrasts between a plover and a sandpiper
why: Visual fields of the European golden plover (Pluvialis apricaria): frontal fields suited to precision pecking, a wide blind area above the head from a supraorbital aliform bone, large eyes for night feeding. The abstract page I opened gives no degrees; the full paper holds binocular, lateral and blind-sector widths for the golden plover, the nearest measured Pluvialis.

authors: Hadden PW, Pas AE, Cassidy SB, Ober WC
title: The eye of the takahe, Porphyrio hochstetteri
why: First study of the takahe eye: eye orientation and visual field, pupil shape and position, refraction, intraocular pressure and ocular dimensions in three birds. The record's abstract gives axial length (13.67 mm) and intraocular pressure but no visual-field degrees; the full text would give the field and binocular width for the one Porphyrio with a measured field. DOI not confirmed.
get: journal via library; the University of Auckland ResearchSpace record may hold an accepted manuscript

authors: Potier S, Bonadonna F, Kelber A, Martin GR, Isard PF, Dulaurent T, Duriez O
title: Visual abilities in two raptors with different ecology
why: Already on the list for the hawk view; for Milvus it adds the black kite's visual field and binocular width (acuity of Milvus migrans is already logged from Potier 2020). The HAL copy returned an access-denied page. Potier 2018 (10.1242/jeb.177295) may add the kite to a wider raptor comparison.

authors: Horridge GA, Giddings C, Stange G
title: The superposition eye of skipper butterflies
why: Anatomy and optics of the eyes of seven Australian skipper genera (Hesperioidea): angular sensitivity about 6 to 8 deg at the 50% contour, a patch of facets of about 30 deg feeding one receptor. Hylephila phyleus is not named in the abstract; the full paper may give facet counts or interommatidial angles for a skipper. Volume and pages are from my memory of the citation, not the page.
get: journal via library; ANU repository record https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/items/caf63330-6738-4319-85b8-a9086a275ca6
